newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance foresees no equity dilution in next 3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance foresees no equity dilution in next 3 yrs.

text.p: Reliance Industries, India's leading private firm, said on Thursday it didn't expect to have any further equity dilution during the next two to three years.

"We do not foresee any further equity dilution over the next two to three years, excluding outstanding conversions (of debentures)," Dhirubhal Ambani, chairman of the petrochemical and textile giant, said.
He was addressing shareholders at the company's annual general meeting in Bombay, ahead of a board meeting where a keenly-awaited bonus equity issue is expected to be announced.
"The bonus offer reflects our confidence in the future," he said in a statement.
Traders have said they expected the company to announce a bonus ratio of three shares for every five shares held -- the same ratio as the firm's last bonus issue in 1983.
But some hope Reliance -- which began as a commodities trading firm in 1958 and built itself into India's largest private company -- would surprise the market with a 1:1 bonus.
Ambani said they expect the company's sales to touch 200 billion rupees ($5.5 billion) by 2000.
"Based on firm plans, our sales are expected to approach the 20,000 crore rupees (200 billion rupees) milestone by the year 2000," he said.
"We have set ourselves targets of achieving 20 percent compound growth in EPS and a return of 20 percent on shareholders funds over the next five years," Ambani said.
